ios.desc:
Productivity systems fail. Todorant works.

Todorant is a to-do list and daily planner that uses behavioral psychology to help you get things done. A carefully tuned set of limits and praise teaches the primitive part of your brain to crave completed tasks the way people crave sugar. Most productivity apps are great at storing, organizing and automating endless lists of tasks, and that is exactly where they fail you, because a list that keeps growing doesn't get anything done. Todorant cares about the one thing that matters, which is finishing what you planned.

It does that with four simple rules:

— Focus on one task at a time. The Current screen shows only the todo you should be doing right now, so you never stare at a wall of tasks wondering where to start.
— Always add a date or a month to a task. Every todo gets its place in time, so nothing lingers forever in a "someday" list that you never open.
— Complete unpleasant tasks first. Mark the todos you dread as frogs and Todorant puts them before everything else on their day, so you eat the frog while your willpower is still fresh.
— Keep your inbox empty. Overdue todos have to be planned again before you can get back to work, so you always know what to do now and when everything else will be done.

What's inside:

— Real-time sync between your iPhone, iPad and the web app at todorant.com, with offline support and conflict resolution that keeps changes made on two devices at once.
— End-to-end encryption of your todos with a password of your choice.
— Delegation, to hand todos to friends and colleagues and accept the ones they hand to you.
— Hashtags and epics to group related work, and reports of everything you've completed.
— A home screen widget with your current todo, and a daily reminder to plan your day at the time you choose.
— A share extension that turns text and links from other apps into todos.
— A Telegram bot that turns messages into todos.
— 22 languages that follow your device, and a dark mode.
— Your own server, if you prefer: Todorant is open source and you can host it yourself in a couple of minutes, then point the app at it from Settings.

Why does it work?

Todorant grew out of more than twenty productivity books and methodologies. Each of them either lacked something important or was too complicated to stick with, so the parts that worked were combined and simplified into a single system that you can learn in a minute. android.desc:
Todorant is a to-do list, task manager and daily planner that uses behavioral psychology to help you get things done. Most productivity apps are great at storing, organizing and automating endless lists of tasks, and that is exactly where they fail you, because a list that keeps growing doesn't get anything done. Todorant cares about the one thing that matters, which is finishing what you planned. It does that with four simple rules, backed by a carefully tuned set of limits and praise that makes finishing todos feel rewarding:
  • Focus on one task at a time. The Current screen shows only the todo you should be doing right now.
  • Always add a date or a month to a task. Every todo gets its place in time, so nothing lingers in a list forever.
  • Complete unpleasant tasks first. Todos you dread are marked as frogs and come before everything else on their day, so you eat the frog while your willpower is fresh and procrastination never gets a foothold.
  • Keep your inbox empty. Overdue todos have to be planned again before you can get back to work.
Your todos sync in real time between your devices and todorant.com, keep working offline, and can be end-to-end encrypted with a password of your choice. Delegation lets you hand todos to friends and colleagues and accept the ones they hand to you, hashtags and epics group related work, and reports show everything you've done. A home screen widget keeps your current todo in sight, a daily reminder tells you when it's time to plan, and the app speaks 22 languages, follows your device's language and has a dark mode. You can use Todorant without an account and keep everything on your phone, or sign in with an email and a password, with Apple, with Telegram or with a QR code from todorant.com. If you'd rather keep your data on your own machine, you can run your own Todorant server in a couple of minutes and point the app at it from the settings. Todorant is free, with no ads and no subscriptions.

quotes.text:
Hello HN! I'm here to show you my latest project — Todorant. It uses cognitive psychology, carefully crafted limits and praise to trick the primitive brain into craving productivity like we crave sugar.

It is available on web (https://todorant.com), iOS (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/todorant/id1482078243) and Android (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.todorant). I've built it all by myself and I'm pretty proud of it :) it is the first project of such enormous scale that I launched solo.

A bit on my background: I've been struggling with productivity all my life until I took a turn towards reading more non-fiction. In the beginning of 2019 I red over 20 productivity and self-help books (some of them were useful, some of them were "meh") and tried to follow the methodologies they described.

Needless to say, I failed every single time.

Since I like to disassemble things and look into how systems work, I took concepts from books I've read and divided them in three groups: advice that helps productivity, advice that does nothing, advice that hurts productivity (e.g. when effort is not worth the productivity gain or when gain is negative).

So I combined concepts that work from various methodologies and simplified the resulting system. I got a simple set of rules that I described in the article "How I launched 7 products in 1 year" (https://medium.com/@nikitakolmogorov/how-i-launched-7-products-in-1-year-efe542b1f8b6).
